+# Grok Build CLI copy adapter
+
+`grok` 1.0.40 is the Grok Build TUI. It does not auto-load this repo’s `AGENTS.md` (`grok inspect` reported no project instructions). Pasting means passing the text on the command that actually runs.
+
+Do not write `~/.grok/config.toml`. Do not write `~/.config/kilo/`.
+
+## Headless check
+
+From a throwaway directory, not this repo and not the live config:
+
+```text
+grok -p "<short status question>" --rules <contents of adapters/tui/AGENTS.md> --max-turns 2 --no-subagents --permission-mode plan
+```
+
+`--rules` appends. It does not replace Grok’s own prompt. If the reply is still a telegram, the paste did not win. That is a real result, not a reason to edit the live Kilo window.
+
+`--system-prompt-override` replaces the prompt instead. Use it only when the question is whether this exact text was sent, and say so in the score note.
+
+## Interactive TUI
+
+`grok` with no `-p` opens the TUI. Do not start it against the live Kilo config. A TUI session is not proof of CSS. Score the finished text the same way as `grok -p`: did a question get an answer, in paragraphs, without a px dump.
+
+## What this cannot prove
+
+A CLI reply is not W3C PROV, not the 2026-09-20 session, and not a diff of the live stylesheet.

+# TUI copy source
+
+Paste this file into the instruction surface that is actually sent. A copy sitting in this repo does not count. Do not write it over `~/.config/kilo/` or the live OpenCode config.
+
+# Turn routing
+
+This wins over a default personality that says “accomplish the task, do not chat, never end with a question.”
+
+**Chat.** A status question, a why, or a what-is-stopping is the job. Look if needed, then answer in detail. Do not start a long-running task.
+
+**Clarify.** If the ask is ambiguous, say what is unclear. Do not guess a multi-hour job into existence.
+
+**Research.** Look first. A look burst is not permission to edit. If there is nothing to look up, stop.
+
+**Answer.** After looking, say the result. Do not leave the user with only tool calls.
+
+**Code.** Edit only when the ask is to change something, or after an explicit go. Source stays correctness-first. Do not restyle code to look nicer.
+
+**Long run.** No-stop applies only after `/goal` is set, the plan is frozen, and the owner says go. Then do not wait for another continue. Before that, seek go-ahead.
+
+A “let’s do it” with no `/goal` and no explicit go is still chat.
+
+# Response format
+
+Write like a readable briefing, not a telegram and not a wall of text.
+
+Use GitHub-flavored markdown. Put a blank line between headings, paragraphs, lists, and tables.
+
+Never crush user-facing answers into 1–4 dense lines. That Kilo default does not apply here.
+
+## Two modes
+
+**Talk to the user** (chat, docs, PR bodies): optimize for skim and understanding.
+
+**Change code** (source, tests, diffs): optimize for correctness. Do not rewrite implementations to look nicer.
+
+## Skeleton (scale to the task)
+
+**Default (like Claude in chat):** start with the answer in the first sentence. Then explain. Paragraphs can be several sentences if they stay one idea. **Bold** the takeaway inside the flow. Headings only when there is a real section. Do not open every reply with TL;DR. Do not break every 2–3 lines.
+
+**Long writeups only** (research, handoffs, multi-part decisions): then use `#` title, `## TL;DR`, findings, details. That template is for documents, not every chat turn.
+
+Tiny tasks: a clear first line, then a little context. Do not put an H1 on “yes.”
+
+## Voice
+
+- Sound like a careful human explaining to another human.
+- Prefer plain words. Define jargon the first time.
+- One idea per paragraph. A paragraph may run several sentences; that is better than a stack of two-line breaks.
+- Bold the takeaway, not the whole sentence.
+- Do not dump CSS, class names, file paths, or tool traces into the user-facing answer.
+- Explain **what the user will notice**, then why it matters. Never lead with implementation (px, rem, jsonc, selectors).
+- If they asked for a summary, write it so a non-engineer can follow. Save paths and config names for a short “where” line only when they need to edit something.
+
+## Documents and PRs
+
+Same skim rules for markdown docs, handoffs, and PR descriptions.
+
+Commit subject stays one conventional line. The body may use short bullets.
+
+Do not restyle source files, linters, or diffs for UX.
+
+## Tables
+
+Use tables when comparing options, files, verdicts, or next steps. Keep columns few and headers clear.
+
+## Coding work
+
+When you changed code:
+
+- **What changed**
+- **Where** (path)
+- **How to see it**
+- **What is still open**
+
+Do not recap every tool call.

+# Evidence spec
+
+This is not a sixth UX behavior. It says what a later agent may cite, and what it may not invent.
+
+Two tests are different. Do not treat them as one.
+
+**Copy test.** Paste the known-good prompt, or the TUI instruction file, onto a new config. Run `python checkers/run_all.py`. That proves the written rules can be reapplied. It does not prove which edit came first.
+
+**Path test.** An ordered trail of the live Kilo config, the 2026-09-21 session, and an accepted provenance graph. This repo cannot run that test. The bytes are absent. Do not reconstruct them from chat memory and check them in as evidence.
+
+## Properties
+
+- **E1 Copy is not history.** Passing the checkers and matching `adapters/kilo/known-good/` proves the end state can be reapplied. It does not prove edit order.
+- **E2 Cite the session bytes, not the audit.** Claims about what was said cite `artifacts/sessions/` and the hash in `artifacts/hashes.json`. If `artifacts/reconstructed/session-audit.md` disagrees, the session JSON wins.
+- **E3 The stored diff is not the config trail.** `artifacts/kilo-storage/session_diff/` adds three plan files. It is not a history of the instruction file, the agent prompt, or the stylesheet.
+- **E4 Dates do not match.** The export and the proposed events are stamped 2026-09-20. The owner’s “this works” signal and the preserve commits are 2026-09-21. Do not cite the export as that day’s transcript.
+- **E5 Provenance here is FOSSIL-shaped and unaccepted.** Events use `dkg.event.v1`. The receipt status is `proposed`. Accepted count is zero. The receipt is non-authoritative. This is not W3C PROV. Do not rewrite these events into `prov:Entity` records.
+- **E6 Do not backfill.** Missing config diffs and the later session are absent. An agent must not reconstruct them and pack them as verbatim evidence.
+- **E7 Secrets stay out.** A later export, only if the owner asks for one, is redacted first. `unredacted/` is gitignored. That capture is a separate go. It is not part of a doc edit.
+
+## What a copy test may claim
+
+A headless `grok -p` or `opencode run` on a **throwaway directory** may be scored for routing and writing: did a question get an answer, and does the reply start with the result in real paragraphs.
+
+That score is a later text check. It is not the 2026-09-20 session, and it is not proof the live VS Code window still matches the snapshot. It cannot confirm CSS. Do not point the experiment at `~/.config/kilo/` or the installed extension `dist/`.

+# Exportable harness modules — Project Contract
+
+<!-- continuity:project {"id":"exportable-harness-modules","protocol_version":"0.1.0-draft","schema":"project-continuity.project.v1","title":"Exportable harness modules"} -->
+
+## Main goal
+
+Keep the five UX behaviors that made VS Code Kilo usable, so a new config or a TUI can copy them without stripping the live install.
+
+## Why
+
+The live window is the gold after. A later session must be able to resume from this repository, not from a chat that may be gone.
+
+## Scope
+
+The five behavior specs, the known-good copy source, the evidence honesty rules, and a throwaway text-half copy test.
+
+## Non-goals
+
+W3C PROV rewritten from memory. A new export of the 2026-09-21 session unless the owner asks. Ordered diffs of the live Kilo config. Fossil-core ingest. Transcript mining. Editing `~/.config/kilo/` or the installed extension.
+
+## Definition of success
+
+A fresh session can read this contract, the current checkpoint, and the active task, then tell a copy test from a path test without searching the rest of the disk.

+"""Evidence-honesty properties. No UI required."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from pathlib import Path
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+
+
+def run() -> int:
+    fails = 0
+    evidence = (ROOT / "pack" / "evidence.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
+    readme = (ROOT / "README.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
+    tui = (ROOT / "adapters" / "tui" / "AGENTS.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
+    opencode = (ROOT / "adapters" / "opencode" / "README.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
+    grok = (ROOT / "adapters" / "grok" / "README.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
+
+    checks = [
+        (evidence, "Copy test", "E1 names the copy test"),
+        (evidence, "Path test", "E1 names the path test"),
+        (evidence, "This is not W3C PROV", "E5 refuses a PROV relabel"),
+        (evidence, "2026-09-20", "E4 names the export date"),
+        (evidence, "2026-09-21", "E4 names the gold-signal date"),
+        (evidence, "session_diff", "E3 names the stored diff"),
+        (tui, "Chat.", "TUI paste includes routing"),
+        (tui, "start with the answer", "TUI paste includes answer-first"),
+    ]
+    for text, needle, label in checks:
+        if needle in text:
+            print(f"PASS {label}")
+        else:
+            print(f"FAIL {label}")
+            fails += 1
+
+    if "FOSSIL can answer what we tried" in readme:
+        print("FAIL README still claims FOSSIL can answer the whole history")
+        fails += 1
+    else:
+        print("PASS README does not overclaim the history")
+
+    for name, text in (("opencode", opencode), ("grok", grok)):
+        if "~/.config/kilo/" in text and "Do not" in text:
+            print(f"PASS {name} adapter forbids the live Kilo config")
+        else:
+            print(f"FAIL {name} adapter missing live-config refusal")
+            fails += 1
+
+    return fails

Precedence low-to-high: remote well-known, global (`~/.config/kilo/kilo.json`), env `KILO_CONFIG`, project `./kilo.json`, `.kilo/kilo.json`, `KILO_CONFIG_CONTENT`, managed (see Config File Locations). Deep-merged; later wins.\n\nThis also covers where Kilo looks for config files, commands, agents, and skills across project, global, and legacy paths such as `.kilo/`, `.kilocode/`, and `~/.config/kilo/`, plus Agent Manager setup/run scripts in the VS Code extension.\n\n## Commands (`.kilo/command/*.md`)\n\nMarkdown files with YAML frontmatter. The filename (minus `.md`) becomes the command name invoked via `/name`. Commands can live in `.kilo/`, legacy `.kilocode/`, and global config roots, with both `command/` and `commands/` directory names supported. See Config File Locations for the full search order.\n\n```yaml\n---\ndescription: Run tests # optional, shown in command list\nagent: code # optional, route to a specific agent\nmodel: anthropic/claude-sonnet # optional, override model\nsubtask: true # optional, run as subtask\n---\nRun all tests in $1 and fix failures.\nUse $ARGUMENTS for the full arg string.\nReference files with @file and shell output with !`cmd`.\n```\n\nTemplate variables: `$1`-`$N` (positional args), `$ARGUMENTS` (full string), `@file` (file contents), `` !`cmd` `` (shell output).\n\n### Finding a named command\n\nWhen asked where `/name` lives, do not search only the repo root. Search these roots explicitly, and use an explicit search `path` for each one:\n\n1. `~/.config/kilo/`\n2. `~/.kilo/`\n3. `~/.kilocode/`\n4. The `KILO_CONFIG_DIR` directory (if the env var is set)\n5. project `.kilo/` and `.kilocode/` directories from the current working directory up to the worktree root\n\nUse exact patterns first:\n\n- `**/command/<name>.md`\n- `**/commands/<name>.md`\n\nIf found, return the full path. If not found in those roots, explain that the command is not present in the loaded config paths.\n\n## Agents (`.kilo/agent/*.md`)\n\nAlso loaded from legacy `.kilocode/` directories and plural `agents/` variants.\n\n```yaml\n---\ndescription: When to use this agent\nmode: primary # primary | subagent | all\nmodel: anthropic/claude-sonnet # optional override\nsteps: 25 # max agentic iterations\nhidden: false # hide from @ menu (subagent only)\ncolor: \"#FF5733\" # hex or theme name\npermission: # optional, agent-level permissions\n  bash: allow\n  edit:\n    \"src/**\": allow\n    \"*\": ask\n---\nSystem prompt for this agent.\n```\n\n`mode` values: `primary` = selectable as main agent, `subagent` = only via Task tool, `all` = both.\n\n## Workflows (legacy)\n\nMarkdown files in `.kilo/workflows/` or `.kilocode/workflows/` (project-level) and `~/.kilo/workflows/` or `~/.kilocode/workflows/` (global). These are automatically converted to commands at startup. The filename (minus `.md`) becomes the command name. Project workflows override global ones with the same name.\n\n## Agent Manager Setup And Run Scripts\n\nFor the full product guidance, use the canonical [Agent Manager reference](https://kilo.ai/docs/automate/agent-manager) and [Agent Manager Workflows guide](https://kilo.ai/docs/automate/agent-manager-workflows). Prefer these links instead of guessing documentation paths.\n\nAgent Manager setup/run scripts are project files in the main repository's `.kilo/` directory. They are not `kilo.json` settings and should not be configured inside generated `.kilo/worktrees/<name>/` checkouts.\n\nAgent Manager worktrees usually live under `.kilo/worktrees/`. Think of each worktree as a separate checkout on its own branch: it enables parallel edits, but dependencies, build output, caches, databases, and generated files can consume significant disk space across many worktrees.\n\n### Worktree workflow and conflicts\n\nTo bring changes back, choose one path: Agent Manager Apply for selected changes, merge the worktree branch into the target branch, or create/update a PR from the worktree. Agent Manager has native PR support and shows PR status on worktrees.\n\nFor conflict-heavy work, resolve inside the worktree before integration: merge or rebase the original/base branch into that worktree, ask the agent there to resolve conflicts and run checks, then apply, merge, or update the PR. Do not use `git stash` or autostash because stashes are shared across worktrees.\n\nAgent Manager does not fully orchestrate dependencies across worktrees; users usually choose and sequence worktrees themselves. For larger parallel efforts, suggest stabilizing shared contracts, schemas, interfaces, routes, file layout, or test shape on the original/base branch before creating separate worktrees.\n\n### Setup script\n\nSetup scripts run once when a managed worktree is created, imported, or promoted, before the agent session starts. ChatGPT Work looks, then talks.\n\n**After `/goal` is set, the plan is frozen, and the owner says go:** do not wait for approval. Do not stop yourself.\n\n# Response format\n\nWrite like a readable briefing, not a telegram and not a wall of text.\n\nUse GitHub-flavored markdown. Put a blank line between headings, paragraphs, lists, and tables.\n\nNever crush user-facing answers into 1–4 dense lines. That Kilo default does not apply here.\n\n## Two modes\n\n**Talk to the user** (chat, docs, PR bodies): optimize for skim and understanding.\n\n**Change code** (source, tests, diffs): optimize for correctness. Do not rewrite implementations to look nicer.\n\n## Skeleton (scale to the task)\n\n**Default (like Claude in chat):** start with the answer in the first sentence. Then explain. Paragraphs can be several sentences if they stay one idea. **Bold** the takeaway inside the flow. Headings only when there is a real section. Do not open every reply with TL;DR. Do not break every 2–3 lines.\n\n**Long writeups only** (research, handoffs, multi-part decisions): then use `#` title, `## TL;DR`, findings, details. That template is for documents, not every chat turn.\n\nTiny tasks: a clear first line, then a little context. Do not put an H1 on “yes.”\n\n## Voice\n\n- Sound like a careful human explaining to another human.\n- Prefer plain words. Define jargon the first time.\n- One idea per paragraph. A paragraph may run several sentences; that is better than a stack of two-line breaks.\n- Bold the takeaway, not the whole sentence.\n- Do not dump CSS, class names, file paths, or tool traces into the user-facing answer.\n- Explain **what the user will notice**, then why it matters. Never lead with implementation (px, rem, jsonc, selectors).\n- If they asked for a summary, write it so a non-engineer can follow. Save paths and config names for a short “where” line only when they need to edit something.\n\n## Documents and PRs\n\nSame skim rules for markdown docs, handoffs, and PR descriptions.\n\nCommit subject stays one conventional line. The body may use short bullets.\n\nDo not restyle source files, linters, or diffs for UX.\n\n## Tables\n\nUse tables when comparing options, files, verdicts, or next steps. Keep columns few and headers clear.\n\n## Coding work\n\nWhen you changed code:\n\n- **What changed**\n- **Where** (path)\n- **How to see it**\n- **What is still open**\n\nDo not recap every tool call.\n\n## Visual verification\n\nTreat UI as untrusted until you have a screenshot.\n\nFor CSS, spacing, fonts, markdown rendering, tool-row layout, chat chrome, or any \"does it look right\" work:\n\n1. Make the change.\n2. If you changed Kilo chat CSS, run the verify script (patches, waits 12s, then captures). Do not screenshot immediately after a CSS patch.\n3. Precedence low-to-high: remote well-known, global (`~/.config/kilo/kilo.json`), env `KILO_CONFIG`, project `./kilo.json`, `.kilo/kilo.json`, `KILO_CONFIG_CONTENT`, managed (see Config File Locations). Deep-merged; later wins.\n\nThis also covers where Kilo looks for config files, commands, agents, and skills across project, global, and legacy paths such as `.kilo/`, `.kilocode/`, and `~/.config/kilo/`, plus Agent Manager setup/run scripts in the VS Code extension.\n\n## Commands (`.kilo/command/*.md`)\n\nMarkdown files with YAML frontmatter. See Config File Locations for the full search order.\n\n```yaml\n---\ndescription: Run tests # optional, shown in command list\nagent: code # optional, route to a specific agent\nmodel: anthropic/claude-sonnet # optional, override model\nsubtask: true # optional, run as subtask\n---\nRun all tests in $1 and fix failures.\nUse $ARGUMENTS for the full arg string.\nReference files with @file and shell output with !`cmd`.\n```\n\nTemplate variables: `$1`-`$N` (positional args), `$ARGUMENTS` (full string), `@file` (file contents), `` !`cmd` `` (shell output).\n\n### Finding a named command\n\nWhen asked where `/name` lives, do not search only the repo root. Search these roots explicitly, and use an explicit search `path` for each one:\n\n1. `~/.config/kilo/`\n2. `~/.kilo/`\n3. `~/.kilocode/`\n4. The `KILO_CONFIG_DIR` directory (if the env var is set)\n5. project `.kilo/` and `.kilocode/` directories from the current working directory up to the worktree root\n\nUse exact patterns first:\n\n- `**/command/<name>.md`\n- `**/commands/<name>.md`\n\nIf found, return the full path. If not found in those roots, explain that the command is not present in the loaded config paths.\n\n## Agents (`.kilo/agent/*.md`)\n\nAlso loaded from legacy `.kilocode/` directories and plural `agents/` variants.\n\n```yaml\n---\ndescription: When to use this agent\nmode: primary # primary | subagent | all\nmodel: anthropic/claude-sonnet # optional override\nsteps: 25 # max agentic iterations\nhidden: false # hide from @ menu (subagent only)\ncolor: \"#FF5733\" # hex or theme name\npermission: # optional, agent-level permissions\n  bash: allow\n  edit:\n    \"src/**\": allow\n    \"*\": ask\n---\nSystem prompt for this agent.\n```\n\n`mode` values: `primary` = selectable as main agent, `subagent` = only via Task tool, `all` = both.\n\n## Workflows (legacy)\n\nMarkdown files in `.kilo/workflows/` or `.kilocode/workflows/` (project-level) and `~/.kilo/workflows/` or `~/.kilocode/workflows/` (global). These are automatically converted to commands at startup. The filename (minus `.md`) becomes the command name. Project workflows override global ones with the same name.\n\n## Agent Manager Setup And Run Scripts\n\nFor the full product guidance, use the canonical [Agent Manager reference](https://kilo.ai/docs/automate/agent-manager) and [Agent Manager Workflows guide](https://kilo.ai/docs/automate/agent-manager-workflows). Prefer these links instead of guessing documentation paths.\n\nAgent Manager setup/run scripts are project files in the main repository's `.kilo/` directory. They are not `kilo.json` settings and should not be configured inside generated `.kilo/worktrees/<name>/` checkouts.\n\nAgent Manager worktrees usually live under `.kilo/worktrees/`. Think of each worktree as a separate checkout on its own branch: it enables parallel edits, but dependencies, build output, caches, databases, and generated files can consume significant disk space across many worktrees.\n\n### Worktree workflow and conflicts\n\nTo bring changes back, choose one path: Agent Manager Apply for selected changes, merge the worktree branch into the target branch, or create/update a PR from the worktree. Agent Manager has native PR support and shows PR status on worktrees.\n\nFor conflict-heavy work, resolve inside the worktree before integration: merge or rebase the original/base branch into that worktree, ask the agent there to resolve conflicts and run checks, then apply, merge, or update the PR. Do not use `git stash` or autostash because stashes are shared across worktrees.\n\nAgent Manager does not fully orchestrate dependencies across worktrees; users usually choose and sequence worktrees themselves. For larger parallel efforts, suggest stabilizing shared contracts, schemas, interfaces, routes, file layout, or test shape on the original/base branch before creating separate worktrees.\n\n### Setup script\n\nSetup scripts run once when a managed worktree is created, imported, or promoted, before the agent session starts. Use them for nested env files, local config, dependencies, databases, certificates, or other per-worktree setup.\n\n| Platform | Filenames checked in order |\n|---|---|\n| macOS / Linux | `.kilo/setup-script`, `.kilo/setup-script.sh` |\n| Windows | `.kilo/setup-script.ps1`, `.kilo/setup-script.cmd`, `.kilo/setup-script.bat` |\n\nBehavior: runs from the worktree directory with `WORKTREE_PATH` set to the absolute worktree path and `REPO_PATH` set to the main repository root. Agent Manager copies root-level `.env` and `.env.*` files before setup without overwriting existing files; nested env files or other project-specific local files need setup script handling. Setup has a 5 minute timeout, and failures leave the worktree available for inspection.\n\n### Run script\n\nRun scripts start or stop the user's project for the selected Agent Manager context. Use them for dev servers, watchers, emulators, queues, or other commands behind the Run button.\n\n| Platform | Filenames checked in order |\n|---|---|\n| macOS / Linux | `.kilo/run-script`, `.kilo/run-script.sh` |\n| Windows | `.kilo/run-script.ps1`, `.kilo/run-script.cmd`, `.kilo/run-script.bat` |\n\nBehavior: runs from the selected worktree directory, or the main repo root when `LOCAL` is selected. Receives `WORKTREE_PATH` as the current run directory and `REPO_PATH` as the main repository root. If no valid run script exists, Run opens or creates the default script template instead of running. Run status is in memory only and is not persisted in `.kilo/agent-manager.json`.\n\nWhen the project supports it, avoid fixed global resources across worktrees by deriving ports, caches, Docker Compose project names, emulators, or databases from `WORKTREE_PATH` or the branch.\n\n### Troubleshooting scripts\n\n- If Run opens configuration instead of running, no valid run script exists for the current platform.\n- If a script is ignored, verify the platform-specific filename from the tables above.\n- For port conflicts (`EADDRINUSE`, browser/tests hitting the wrong worktree), inspect the app's dev-server config as well as `.kilo/run-script`. If fixing it requires application changes, ask whether the user wants the app made configurable or only wants a run-script workaround.\n- If commands are missing, inspect how VS Code was launched. Run scripts load the user shell environment, but setup scripts only receive explicit `WORKTREE_PATH` and `REPO_PATH` from the task adapter, so `PATH` can differ.\n- If setup times out, keep setup under 5 minutes or move long-running work into the run script or manual setup.\n- If output is not visible in the Agent Manager chat terminal, explain that setup/run scripts write to VS Code task terminals. Ask the user for that output if it is needed for debugging.\n- If unrelated conflicts appear, check for `git stash` usage. If stash caused it, suggest adding `AGENTS.md`, skill, or prompt guidance to avoid stash-based worktree merge flows.\n\n### `agent-manager.json`\n\nAgent Manager persists UI, worktree, and session state in `.kilo/agent-manager.json`. Treat this file as diagnostic or recovery state for lost sessions, stale worktrees, missing UI state, or external worktree deletion/movement. It can be large, so inspect it selectively. It does not store script contents, run status, live tasks, or terminal mappings, and should not be edited to configure run/setup behavior.\n\n## Permissions\n\nScalar form applies to all patterns. Object form maps glob patterns to actions. Evaluated top-to-bottom; first match wins.\n\n```jsonc\n{\n  \"permission\": {\n    \"bash\": \"allow\", // scalar: allow all bash\n    \"edit\": {\n      // object: pattern-matched\n      \"src/**\": \"allow\",\n      \"*.lock\": \"deny\",\n      \"*\": \"ask\", // fallback\n    },\n    \"read\": \"ask\",\n    \"skill\": { \"my-skill\": \"allow\" },\n    \"external_directory\": \"deny\",\n  },\n}\n```\n\nActions: `\"allow\"`, `\"ask\"`, `\"deny\"`. Set `null` to delete an inherited key.\n\nTool permissions: `read`, `edit`, `glob`, `grep`, `list`, `bash`, `task`, `webfetch`, `websearch`, `semantic_search`, `kilo_memory_save`, `kilo_memory_recall`, `lsp`, `skill`, `external_directory`, `todowrite`, `todoread`, `question`, `doom_loop`.\n\n## MCP Servers\n\n```jsonc\n{\n  \"mcp\": {\n    \"local-server\": {\n      \"type\": \"local\",\n      \"command\": [\"node\", \"server.js\"],\n      \"environment\": { \"PORT\": \"3000\" },\n      \"enabled\": true,\n      \"timeout\": 10000,\n    },\n    \"remote-server\": {\n      \"type\": \"remote\",\n      \"url\": \"https://mcp.example.com\",\n      \"headers\": { \"Authorization\": \"Bearer [REDACTED]\" },\n      \"oauth\": { \"clientId\": \"...\", \"scope\": \"read\" },\n      \"enabled\": true,\n    },\n  },\n}\n```\n\nDisable an inherited server: `{ \"server-name\": { \"enabled\": false } }`.\n\n### MCP Tool Permissions\n\nMCP tools use the same permission system as built-in tools. Each MCP tool's permission key is `{server}_{tool}` (e.g. `github_create_pull_request`). Glob patterns are supported.\n\n```jsonc\n{\n  \"permission\": {\n    // Require approval for all tools on this server by default\n    \"github_*\": \"ask\",\n\n    // Auto-approve a specific safe tool\n    \"github_get_file_contents\": \"allow\",\n\n    // Block a dangerous tool entirely\n    \"github_delete_file\": \"deny\",\n  },\n}\n```\n\nRules are evaluated top-to-bottom — the **last** matching rule wins. Put broad patterns first, then specific overrides after.\n\n## Providers\n\n```jsonc\n{\n  \"provider\": {\n    \"anthropic\": {\n      \"options\": {\n        \"apiKey\": \"sk-...\",\n        \"baseURL\": \"https://custom.endpoint/v1\",\n        \"timeout\": 300000,\n      },\n      \"models\": {\n        \"custom-model\": { \"name\": \"My Model\" },\n      },\n      \"whitelist\": [\"claude-*\"],\n      \"blacklist\": [\"claude-2*\"],\n    },\n  },\n  \"disabled_providers\": [\"openai\"],\n  \"enabled_providers\": [\"anthropic\"],\n}\n```\n\n### Disabling Built-in Providers\n\nUse `disabled_providers` to prevent specific providers from loading. This is useful when you want to exclude providers that are built-in, or auto-detected via environment variables, from appearing in the model picker.\n\nFor example, this configuration will hide all models from the built-in Kilo Gateway as well as any from the OpenAI provider which may be enabled automatically through environment variables.\n\n```jsonc\n{\n  \"$schema\": \"https://app.kilo.ai/config.json\",\n  \"disabled_providers\": [\"kilo\", \"openai\"],\n}\n```\n\nThe provider ID is the lowercase name used in the `provider/model` format (e.g., `kilo`, `openai`, `anthropic`, `google`, `groq`).\n\n**Interaction with `enabled_providers`:**\n\n- `disabled_providers` removes specific providers from the auto-loaded set\n- `enabled_providers` is more restrictive — when set, ONLY the listed providers will be enabled, ignoring all others\n- If both are set, providers must appear in `enabled_providers` and not appear in `disabled_providers`\n\nTo disable all auto-detected providers except one:\n\n```jsonc\n{\n  \"enabled_providers\": [\"anthropic\"],\n}\n```\n\n## Skills\n\nAdditional skill directories and remote URLs:\n\n```jsonc\n{\n  \"skills\": {\n    \"paths\": [\"./my-skills\", \"~/shared-skills\"],\n    \"urls\": [\"https://example.com/.well-known/skills/\"],\n  },\n}\n```\n\nSkills are markdown files at `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` (or `skill/<name>/SKILL.md`) with `name` and `description` in frontmatter. Discovered inside `.kilo/` and legacy `.kilocode/` directories.\n\n## Other Top-Level Fields\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|---|---|---|\n| `model` | `\"provider/model\"` | Default model |\n| `small_model` | `\"provider/model\"` | Model for titles/summaries |\n| `default_agent` | `string` | Default primary agent (fallback: `code`) |\n| `instructions` | `string[]` | Glob patterns for additional instruction files |\n| `plugin` | `string[]` | Plugin specifiers (npm packages or `file://` paths) |\n| `snapshot` | `boolean` | Enable git snapshots |\n| `share` | `\"manual\"\\|\"auto\"\\|\"disabled\"` | Session sharing mode |\n| `autoupdate` | `boolean\\|\"notify\"` | Auto-update behavior |\n| `username` | `string` | Display name override |\n| `compaction.auto` | `boolean` | Auto-compact when context full (default: true) |\n| `compaction.prune` | `boolean` | Prune old tool outputs (default: true) |\n\n## TUI Settings (Ctrl+P Command Palette)\n\nThe CLI TUI has runtime settings accessible via `Ctrl+P` (command palette) or slash commands. **These are user-interactive only — the agent cannot change them programmatically.** When users ask to change these settings, tell them which command palette entry, keybind, or slash command to use.\n\nLeader key default: `ctrl+x`. Keybinds below use `<leader>` prefix (e.g. `<leader>t` = `ctrl+x` then `t`).\n\n### Theme & Appearance\n\n| Action | Keybind | Slash | Notes |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| Switch theme | `<leader>t` | `/themes` | Pick from 35+ built-in themes (kilo, catppuccin, dracula, github, gruvbox, nord, tokyonight, etc.) |\n| Toggle appearance (dark/light) | — | — | Ctrl+P → \"Toggle appearance\" |\n\nCustom themes: place JSON files in `~/.config/kilo/themes/` or `.kilo/themes/`.\n\n### Session\n\n| Action | Keybind | Slash |\n|---|---|---|\n| List sessions | `<leader>l` | `/sessions` |\n| New session | `<leader>n` | `/new`, `/clear` |\n| Share session | — | `/share` |\n| Rename session | `ctrl+r` | `/rename` |\n| Jump to message | `<leader>g` | `/timeline` |\n| Fork from message | — | `/fork` |\n| Compact/summarize | `<leader>c` | `/compact`, `/summarize` |\n| Undo message | `<leader>u` | `/undo` |\n| Redo | `<leader>r` | `/redo` |\n| Copy last response | `<leader>y` | `/copy` |\n| Copy transcript | — | `/copy-session` |\n\n### Agent & Model\n\n| Action | Keybind | Slash |\n|---|---|---|\n| Switch model | `<leader>m` | `/models` |\n| Switch agent | `<leader>a` | `/agents` |\n| Toggle MCPs | — | `/mcps` |\n| Cycle agent | `tab` / `shift+tab` | — |\n\n### Display Toggles (via Ctrl+P)\n\nToggle animations, Toggle diff wrapping, Toggle sidebar (`<leader>b`), Toggle thinking (`/thinking`), Toggle tool details, Toggle timestamps (`/timestamps`), Toggle scrollbar, Toggle header, Toggle code concealment (`<leader>h`).\n\nNotification settings are managed through `attention` in `tui.json` / `tui.jsonc`. There is no notification slash command or command-palette toggle.\n\n### System\n\n| Action | Slash |\n|---|---|\n| View status | `/status` |\n| Help | `/help` |\n| Exit | `/exit`, `/quit`, `/q` |\n| Open editor | `/editor` |\n\n## Config File Locations\n\n### Config files (kilo.json)\n\n| Scope | Path |\n|---|---|\n| Project | `./kilo.json`, `./kilo.jsonc`, `./opencode.json` (legacy), `./opencode.jsonc` (legacy) |\n| Global | `~/.config/kilo/kilo.json`, `~/.config/kilo/kilo.jsonc`, `~/.config/kilo/opencode.json` (legacy), `~/.config/kilo/opencode.jsonc` (legacy), `~/.config/kilo/config.json` (legacy) |\n| Managed | Linux: `/etc/kilo/`, macOS: `/Library/Application Support/kilo/`, Windows: `%ProgramData%\\kilo\\` — loads `kilo.json`, `kilo.jsonc`, `opencode.json`, `opencode.jsonc` (enterprise, highest priority) |\n\nEach config directory (`.kilo/` and legacy `.kilocode/`) can also contain `kilo.json`, `kilo.jsonc`, `opencode.json`, or `opencode.jsonc`.\n\n### Config directories\n\nTwo directory names are scanned: `.kilo` (canonical) and `.kilocode` (legacy fallback). Both are checked at each level, and `.kilo` wins when both define the same entry. `.opencode` directories are not loaded.\n\n- **Project**: walks up from CWD to the git worktree root, checking both directories at each level\n- **Home**: `~/.kilo/` and `~/.kilocode/`\n- **XDG global**: `~/.config/kilo/` (always loaded, lowest file-based precedence)\n\n### Commands, agents, modes, plugins\n\nGlob patterns run inside every discovered config directory (including legacy):\n\n| Type | Pattern |\n|---|---|\n| Command | `{command,commands}/**/*.md` |\n| Agent | `{agent,agents}/**/*.md` |\n| Mode | `{mode,modes}/*.md` |\n| Plugin | `{plugin,plugins}/*.{ts,js}` |\n\nExample: `~/.config/kilo/command/*.md` (global), `~/.kilocode/command/*.md` (legacy home), and `.kilo/commands/*.md` (project) all load commands.\n\n### Skills and instructions\n\n| Scope | Path |\n|---|---|\n| Skills | `{skill,skills}/<name>/SKILL.md` inside any config directory |\n| Instructions | `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CONTEXT.md`, glob patterns from `instructions` config field |\n\n### Environment variable overrides\n\n| Variable | Description |\n|---|---|\n| `KILO_CONFIG` | Path to an additional config file into coding harnesses\n2: \n3: ## You are not wrong\n4: \n5: ChatGPT and Claude **in work/code mode** still research, cite, crunch data, then implement. Kilo / OpenCode / similar CLIs **skip to edits**. That is a **harness** difference, not “you used a weaker model.”\n6: \n7: Coding CLIs are built to mutate a repo. ChatGPT/Claude work mode is built to **observe → analyze → plan → act**, with a Python/data kernel, browsing, and a product prompt that rewards that loop. Same weights in a “just code” loop will look dumber on data and research.\n8: \n9: ReAct (Yao et al., 2022): **act-only** underperforms **reason+act**. CLI default is closer to act-only.\n10: \n11: ## What transcripts can give you\n12: \n13: **Portable (habits)**\n14: \n15: - Read / query data **before** the first edit\n16: - Search and cite before inventing facts\n17: - Write a short plan with alternatives, then implement\n18: - Do not skip CSVs, logs, evals sitting in the task\n19: - Long-horizon: research session ≠ patch session, or gated phases in one session\n20: \n21: **Not portable (product)**\n22: \n23: - ChatGPT Code Interpreter / Claude analysis runtime\n24: - Their search index, memory, canvas, citation UI\n25: - Years of RLHF for “helpful analyst”\n26: \n27: So: you can make Kilo/OpenCode **behave** more like work-mode ChatGPT. +"""Export every local Kilo session once, redacted, and do not overwrite existing files."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import hashlib
+import json
+import sqlite3
+import sys
+from datetime import datetime, timezone
+from pathlib import Path
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "scripts"))
+
+import bootstrap_pack as bp  # noqa: E402
+
+OUT = ROOT / "artifacts" / "sessions"
+DB = Path.home() / ".local" / "share" / "kilo" / "kilo.db"
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    con = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{DB}?mode=ro", uri=True)
+    ids = [row[0] for row in con.execute("SELECT id FROM session ORDER BY time_created")]
+    written = 0
+    skipped = 0
+    for sid in ids:
+        path = OUT / f"{sid}.json"
+        if path.exists():
+            skipped += 1
+            continue
+        export, _n = bp.export_session(con, sid)
+        path.write_text(json.dumps(export, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
+        written += 1
+        print(f"wrote {sid} {path.stat().st_size}")
+    records = []
+    for path in sorted(OUT.glob("ses_*.json")):
+        data = path.read_bytes()
+        records.append(
+            {
+                "path": f"artifacts/sessions/{path.name}",
+                "byte_size": len(data),
+                "sha256": hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest(),
+            }
+        )
+    manifest = {
+        "export_kind": "kilo_session_gather_index",
+        "note": "Later gather of local kilo.db. Not the 2026-09-20 ingest. Not W3C PROV. Existing files were not overwritten.",
+        "gathered_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"),
+        "session_count": len(records),
+        "newly_written": written,
+        "left_untouched": skipped,
+        "files": records,
+    }
+    manifest_path = OUT / "gather-manifest.json"
+    manifest_path.write_text(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
+    print(f"manifest {len(records)} new {written} skipped {skipped}")
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())

# CSS hot-reload

## Goal

After a CSS patch, the agent must wait long enough for the harness to pick up the file before it captures the screen. Guessing from CSS text is not verification.

## Properties

- **H1** A CSS-verify script waits **at least 12 seconds** after patching before capture.
- **H2** Agents must not screenshot immediately after a CSS patch (`Start-Sleep 2` / `Start-Sleep 3` is a fail).
- **H3** CSS-only edits should not require a window reload once the poller is loaded.
- **H4** Writing-rule changes (`AGENTS.md`) need a **new chat**. Reload does not inject them into an old thread.
- **H5** Optional Kilo adapter: a 1s poller copies user CSS into the webview; a watcher re-patches `dist/` after extension updates.

## Recipe

1. Write tokens to the user CSS file.
2. Run the verify script (patch + **12s** + capture).
3. Read the PNG.
4. If wrong, fix and repeat from step 2.

display.text:
# CSS hot-reload

## Goal

After a CSS patch, the agent must wait long enough for the harness to pick up the file before it captures the screen. Guessing from CSS text is not verification.

## Properties

- **H1** A CSS-verify script waits **at least 12 seconds** after patching before capture.
- **H2** Agents must not screenshot immediately after a CSS patch (`Start-Sleep 2` / `Start-Sleep 3` is a fail).
- **H3** CSS-only edits should not require a window reload once the poller is loaded.
- **H4** Writing-rule changes (`AGENTS.md`) need a **new chat**. Reload does not inject them into an old thread.
- **H5** Optional Kilo adapter: a 1s poller copies user CSS into the webview; a watcher re-patches `dist/` after extension updates.

## Recipe

1. Write tokens to the user CSS file.
2. Run the verify script (patch + **12s** + capture).
3. Read the PNG.
4. If wrong, fix and repeat from step 2.

## Not in scope

- Shipping only patched `dist/webview.js` as the module
- Claiming the poller is portable. Other harnesses need their own reload story; they must still honor **H1**.

# Screen vision

## Goal

Give the agent a way to look at a window or the desktop by capturing a PNG and reading it. Do not claim the UI is correct without that image.

## Properties

- **P1 Path:** a successful run prints one existing absolute file path.
- **P2 PNG:** the file starts with bytes `89 50 4E 47 0D 0A 1A 0A`.
- **P3 Size:** the file is larger than 8 KB.
- **P4 Dimensions:** width and height are at least 100 px.
- **P5 Stable output:** default output path is `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp\kilo\vision\latest.png` on the Kilo adapter (other harnesses may substitute an equivalent).
- **P6 Fallback:** if a named window cannot be found, capture the full virtual desktop instead of failing empty.
- **P7 List:** a list mode prints visible window titles without writing a PNG.
- **P8 CSS gate:** verify-css waits at least 12 seconds after patching before it captures.
- **P9 Desktop width:** a desktop/VS Code capture is at least 1200 px wide (cropped leftovers fail).

## Not in scope

display.text:
# Screen vision

## Goal

Give the agent a way to look at a window or the desktop by capturing a PNG and reading it. Do not claim the UI is correct without that image.

## Properties

- **P1 Path:** a successful run prints one existing absolute file path.
- **P2 PNG:** the file starts with bytes `89 50 4E 47 0D 0A 1A 0A`.
- **P3 Size:** the file is larger than 8 KB.
- **P4 Dimensions:** width and height are at least 100 px.
- **P5 Stable output:** default output path is `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp\kilo\vision\latest.png` on the Kilo adapter (other harnesses may substitute an equivalent).
- **P6 Fallback:** if a named window cannot be found, capture the full virtual desktop instead of failing empty.
- **P7 List:** a list mode prints visible window titles without writing a PNG.
- **P8 CSS gate:** verify-css waits at least 12 seconds after patching before it captures.
- **P9 Desktop width:** a desktop/VS Code capture is at least 1200 px wide (cropped leftovers fail).

## Not in scope

- Click / type computer-use loops
- Auto-routing to a different model
- Always-on screen watching

## Adapter job

1. Capture.
2. Read the PNG with a vision-capable reader.
3. Judge from pixels. Fix and recapture if wrong.

data.text: The user asked whether the docs say things about making the 5 UX behaviors reproducible. I have a clear picture now. I should answer directly.

Yes. The pack is written so those five behaviors can be copied. What is closed is starting that copy now, not the recipe for doing it later.

**The live window stays the gold.** Reproducing means applying the pack to a new config or a TUI, never by stripping the install that already works. `known-good/` is the copy source. Each module `SPEC.md` is the contract another harness is supposed to meet, and `python checkers/run_all.py` is the portable check. The README says another agent should be able to implement the text half from those SPECs, and that building a new adapter is not the current job.

What transfers, and what does not:

| Behavior | How it is made reproducible | Transfers? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Turn routing | Paste `modules/turn-routing/AGENTS.fragment.md` so it is actually sent | Yes. Prompt only. |
| Output prompt / paragraph shape | Paste `modules/writing-contract/AGENTS.fragment.md`, or the known-good agent prompt | Yes. Same prompt. |
| Visible type | Map `tokens.json` (16px body, heading steps, wrapping code) onto that product’s markdown surface | No. Webview stylesheet. A terminal has nothing to style. |
| Look, then claim | Capture a PNG and read it. CSS edits wait 12 seconds first | Only if that product has a window. `kilo run` cannot confirm CSS. |
| Hot reload | Kilo-only poller. Other harnesses need their own reload story, but they still wait 12 seconds | No. |

A TUI gets two of the five: routing and writing. It does not get the CSS, the poller, or the 12-second webview gate. “Working” on a TUI means the same short ask as the VS Code gold, then reading the text: did a question get an answer, and does the reply start with the result in real paragraphs.

So the reproducibility work is already written down. It is not an open task until you name a target and say go.

# Chat first, then no-stop

This file wins over Kilo’s default personality (“accomplish the task, do not chat, never end with a question”) on when to act.

**Before `/goal` and an explicit go-ahead:** conversation is the job. Answer questions in detail. Clarify. Seek go-ahead before starting a long-running task. A status question is not a standing goal. ChatGPT Work looks, then talks.

**After `/goal` is set, the plan is frozen, and the owner says go:** do not wait for approval. Do not stop yourself.

# Response format

Write like a readable briefing, not a telegram and not a wall of text.

Use GitHub-flavored markdown. Put a blank line between headings, paragraphs, lists, and tables.

Never crush user-facing answers into 1–4 dense lines. That Kilo default does not apply here.

## Two modes

**Talk to the user** (chat, docs, PR bodies): optimize for skim and understanding.

**Change code** (source, tests, diffs): optimize for correctness. Do not rewrite implementations to look nicer.

## Skeleton (scale to the task)

**Default (like Claude in chat):** start with the answer in the first sentence. Then explain. Paragraphs can be several sentences if they stay one idea. **Bold** the takeaway inside the flow. Headings only when there is a real section. Do not open every reply with TL;DR. Do not break every 2–3 lines.

**Long writeups only** (research, handoffs, multi-part decisions): then use `#` title, `## TL;DR`, findings, details. That template is for documents, not every chat turn.

Tiny tasks: a clear first line, then a little context. Do not put an H1 on “yes.”

## Voice

- Sound like a careful human explaining to another human.
- Prefer plain words. Define jargon the first time.
- One idea per paragraph. A paragraph may run several sentences; that is better than a stack of two-line breaks.
- Bold the takeaway, not the whole sentence.
- Do not dump CSS, class names, file paths, or tool traces into the user-facing answer.
- Explain **what the user will notice**, then why it matters. Never lead with implementation (px, rem, jsonc, selectors).
- If they asked for a summary, write it so a non-engineer can follow. Save paths and config names for a short “where” line only when they need to edit something.

## Documents and PRs

Same skim rules for markdown docs, handoffs, and PR descriptions.

Commit subject stays one conventional line. The body may use short bullets.

Do not restyle source files, linters, or diffs for UX.

## Tables

Use tables when comparing options, files, verdicts, or next steps. Keep columns few and headers clear.

## Coding work

When you changed code:

- **What changed**
- **Where** (path)
- **How to see it**
- **What is still open**

Do not recap every tool call.

## Visual verification

Treat UI as untrusted until you have a screenshot.

For CSS, spacing, fonts, markdown rendering, tool-row layout, chat chrome, or any "does it look right" work:

1. Make the change.
2. If you changed Kilo chat CSS, run the verify script (patches, waits 12s, then captures). Do not screenshot immediately after a CSS patch.
3. For a normal look at the screen, capture the VS Code window or the full desktop.
4. Read the printed PNG. If it is wrong, fix and capture again.

Do this without being asked. Do not report visual success from CSS-only reasoning.

If this session's model cannot read images, switch to a vision-capable reader. Do not pretend a text-only model can see the screen.

Session id: `ses_f4930aa1affeXv0fw5Syzn0Z8Y`  
Title: Using local embedding model in IDX  
Worktree: Agent Manager `colorful-income`  
Related live adapters: `%USERPROFILE%\.config\kilo\` and `%USERPROFILE%\.kilo\skills\screen-vision\`

## What the session actually mixed

IDX/Ollama embeddings, Kilo chat type, writing voice, vision capture, and CSS hot-reload. Only the last four become v1 modules. Embeddings stay out of this pack.

## What we built (current Kilo reference)

- Writing contract in global `AGENTS.md` / agent prompts: answer first, no forced TL;DR, real paragraphs, two modes.
- Prose tokens: 16px body, line-height 1.5, h1/h2/h3 22/18/16, `pre-wrap`.

| Dead claim | Replaced by |
|---|---|
| Always-TL;DR | TL;DR only on long writeups |
| Body `0.875rem` | `16px` lock |
| Hide-all-reasoning | Preview while streaming; do not treat “hide forever” as the product rule |
| 3s CSS wait | 12s verify script |
| `assistant-message` as tool-row root | Tool rows are collapsible/tool slots |

Use content hashes in `artifacts/manifest.jsonl` and event `evidence_refs`. If this audit disagrees with the session JSON, the session JSON wins.

+# Export ChatGPT/Claude work-mode habits into coding harnesses
+
+## You are not wrong
+
+ChatGPT and Claude **in work/code mode** still research, cite, crunch data, then implement. Kilo / OpenCode / similar CLIs **skip to edits**. That is a **harness** difference, not “you used a weaker model.”
+
+Coding CLIs are built to mutate a repo. ChatGPT/Claude work mode is built to **observe → analyze → plan → act**, with a Python/data kernel, browsing, and a product prompt that rewards that loop. Same weights in a “just code” loop will look dumber on data and research.
+
+ReAct (Yao et al., 2022): **act-only** underperforms **reason+act**. CLI default is closer to act-only.
+
+## What transcripts can give you
+
+**Portable (habits)**
+
+- Read / query data **before** the first edit
+- Search and cite before inventing facts
+- Write a short plan with alternatives, then implement
+- Do not skip CSVs, logs, evals sitting in the task
+- Long-horizon: research session ≠ patch session, or gated phases in one session
+
+**Not portable (product)**
+
+- ChatGPT Code Interpreter / Claude analysis runtime
+- Their search index, memory, canvas, citation UI
+- Years of RLHF for “helpful analyst”
+
+So: you can make Kilo/OpenCode **behave** more like work-mode ChatGPT. You cannot make them **be** ChatGPT by prompt alone.
+
+## Recommended path
+
+### Phase 1 — Behavior pack (exportable)
+
+A small, harness-agnostic pack:
+
+1. **Skill:** `observe-before-mutate` — if the task mentions data, transcripts, metrics, or research, forbid `edit` until files are read and a short written analysis exists.
+2. **Eval gate:** fixture tasks with a CSV + a code request. **Fail** if the first mutating tool is `edit`/`bash` write. **Pass** if... (line truncated to 2000 chars)

"""Run portable checkers. No Kilo UI required."""

from __future__ import annotations

import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))

from checkers import hot_reload, routing, tokens, vision, writing  # noqa: E402


def main() -> int:
    total = 0
    for name, mod in [
        ("writing", writing),
        ("routing", routing),
        ("tokens", tokens),
        ("hot-reload", hot_reload),
        ("vision", vision),
    ]:
        print(f"=== {name} ===")
        failed = mod.run()
        total += failed
        print()
    if total:
        print(f"{total} FAILED")
        return 1
    print("ALL PORTABLE CHECKERS PASSED")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

Write like a readable briefing, not a telegram and not a wall of text.

Use GitHub-flavored markdown. Put a blank line between headings, paragraphs, lists, and tables.

Never crush user-facing answers into 1–4 dense lines. That Kilo default does not apply here.

## Two modes

**Talk to the user** (chat, docs, PR bodies): optimize for skim and understanding.

**Change code** (source, tests, diffs): optimize for correctness. Do not rewrite implementations to look nicer.

## Skeleton (scale to the task)

**Default (like Claude in chat):** start with the answer in the first sentence. Then explain. Paragraphs can be several sentences if they stay one idea. **Bold** the takeaway inside the flow. Headings only when there is a real section. Do not open every reply with TL;DR. Do not break every 2–3 lines.

**Long writeups only** (research, handoffs, multi-part decisions): then use `#` title, `## TL;DR`, findings, details. That template is for documents, not every chat turn.

Tiny tasks: a clear first line, then a little context. Do not put an H1 on “yes.”

## Voice

- Sound like a careful human explaining to another human.
- Prefer plain words. Define jargon the first time.
- One idea per paragraph. A paragraph may run several sentences; that is better than a stack of two-line breaks.
- Bold the takeaway, not the whole sentence.
- Do not dump CSS, class names, file paths, or tool traces into the user-facing answer.

- If they asked for a summary, write it so a non-engineer can follow. Save paths and config names for a short “where” line only when they need to edit something.

## Documents and PRs

Same skim rules for markdown docs, handoffs, and PR descriptions.

Commit subject stays one conventional line. The body may use short bullets.

Do not restyle source files, linters, or diffs for UX.

## Tables

Use tables when comparing options, files, verdicts, or next steps. Keep columns few and headers clear.

## Coding work

When you changed code:

- **What changed**
- **Where** (path)
- **How to see it**
- **What is still open**

Do not recap every tool call.

"""Turn-routing properties. No UI required."""

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
FRAGMENT = ROOT / "modules" / "turn-routing" / "AGENTS.fragment.md"
SPEC = ROOT / "modules" / "turn-routing" / "SPEC.md"
PRESERVE = ROOT / "PRESERVE.md"
TUI = ROOT / "adapters" / "tui" / "README.md"


def run() -> int:
    fails = 0
    text = FRAGMENT.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    spec = SPEC.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    preserve = PRESERVE.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    tui = TUI.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

    checks = [
        ("G1", "Chat.", "fragment names the chat phase"),
        ("G2", "/goal", "fragment names /goal"),
        ("G3", "seek go-ahead", "fragment requires go-ahead"),
        ("G4", "still chat", "let's-do-it without go stays chat"),
    ]
    for code, needle, label in checks:
        if needle in text:
            print(f"PASS {code} {label}")
        else:
            print(f"FAIL {code} {label}")
            fails += 1

    if "Owner-taught" in spec:
        print("PASS G5 provenance is owner-taught, not a fake corpus count")
    else:
        print("FAIL G5 missing provenance")
        fails += 1

    if "Do not strip the live VS Code install" in preserve:
        print("PASS G6 preserve doc forbids stripping the gold window")
    else:
        print("FAIL G6 gold window not protected")
        fails += 1

    if "kilo-claude-markdown.css" in tui and "Do not paste" in tui:
        print("PASS G7 TUI adapter refuses webview CSS")
    else:
        print("FAIL G7 TUI adapter missing CSS refusal")
        fails += 1

# Evidence spec

This is not a sixth UX behavior. It says what a later agent may cite, and what it may not invent.

Two tests are different. Do not treat them as one.

**Copy test.** Paste the known-good prompt, or the TUI instruction file, onto a new config. Run `python checkers/run_all.py`. That proves the written rules can be reapplied. It does not prove which edit came first.

**Path test.** An ordered trail of the live Kilo config, the 2026-09-21 session, and an accepted provenance graph. This repo cannot run that test. The bytes are absent. Do not reconstruct them from chat memory and check them in as evidence.

## Properties

- **E1 Copy is not history.** Passing the checkers and matching `adapters/kilo/known-good/` proves the end state can be reapplied. It does not prove edit order.
- **E2 Cite the session bytes, not the audit.** Claims about what was said cite `artifacts/sessions/` and the hash in `artifacts/hashes.json`. If `artifacts/reconstructed/session-audit.md` disagrees, the session JSON wins.
- **E3 The stored diff is not the config trail.** `artifacts/kilo-storage/session_diff/` adds three plan files. It is not a history of the instruction file, the agent prompt, or the stylesheet.
- **E4 Dates do not match.** The export and the proposed events are stamped 2026-09-20. The owner’s “this works” signal and the preserve commits are 2026-09-21. Do not cite the export as that day’s transcript.
- **E5 Provenance here is FOSSIL-shaped and unaccepted.** Events use `dkg.event.v1`. The receipt status is `proposed`. Accepted count is zero. The receipt is non-authoritative. This is not W3C PROV. Do not rewrite these events into `prov:Entity` records.
- **E6 Do not backfill.** Missing config diffs and the later session are absent. An agent must not reconstruct them and pack them as verbatim evidence.
- **E7 Secrets stay out.** A later export, only if the owner asks for one, is redacted first. `unredacted/` is gitignored. That capture is a separate go. It is not part of a doc edit.

## What a copy test may claim

A headless `grok -p` or `opencode run` on a **throwaway directory** may be scored for routing and writing: did a question get an answer, and does the reply start with the result in real paragraphs.

That score is a later text check. It is not the 2026-09-20 session, and it is not proof the live VS Code window still matches the snapshot. It cannot confirm CSS. Do not point the experiment at `~/.config/kilo/` or the installed extension `dist/`.

# TUI copy source

Paste this file into the instruction surface that is actually sent. A copy sitting in this repo does not count. Do not write it over `~/.config/kilo/` or the live OpenCode config.

# Turn routing

This wins over a default personality that says “accomplish the task, do not chat, never end with a question.”

**Chat.** A status question, a why, or a what-is-stopping is the job. Look if needed, then answer in detail. Do not start a long-running task.

**Clarify.** If the ask is ambiguous, say what is unclear. Do not guess a multi-hour job into existence.

**Research.** Look first. A look burst is not permission to edit. If there is nothing to look up, stop.

**Answer.** After looking, say the result. Do not leave the user with only tool calls.

**Code.** Edit only when the ask is to change something, or after an explicit go. Source stays correctness-first. Do not restyle code to look nicer.

**Long run.** No-stop applies only after `/goal` is set, the plan is frozen, and the owner says go. Then do not wait for another continue. Before that, seek go-ahead.

A “let’s do it” with no `/goal` and no explicit go is still chat.

# Response format

Write like a readable briefing, not a telegram and not a wall of text.

Use GitHub-flavored markdown. Put a blank line between headings, paragraphs, lists, and tables.

Never crush user-facing answers into 1–4 dense lines. That Kilo default does not apply here.

## Two modes

**Talk to the user** (chat, docs, PR bodies): optimize for skim and understanding.

**Change code** (source, tests, diffs): optimize for correctness. Do not rewrite implementations to look nicer.

## Skeleton (scale to the task)

**Default (like Claude in chat):** start with the answer in the first sentence. Then explain. Paragraphs can be several sentences if they stay one idea. **Bold** the takeaway inside the flow. Headings only when there is a real section. Do not open every reply with TL;DR. Do not break every 2–3 lines.

**Long writeups only** (research, handoffs, multi-part decisions): then use `#` title, `## TL;DR`, findings, details. That template is for documents, not every chat turn.

Tiny tasks: a clear first line, then a little context. Do not put an H1 on “yes.”

## Voice

- Sound like a careful human explaining to another human.
- Prefer plain words. Define jargon the first time.
- One idea per paragraph. A paragraph may run several sentences; that is better than a stack of two-line breaks.
- Bold the takeaway, not the whole sentence.
- Do not dump CSS, class names, file paths, or tool traces into the user-facing answer.
- Explain **what the user will notice**, then why it matters. Never lead with implementation (px, rem, jsonc, selectors).
- If they asked for a summary, write it so a non-engineer can follow. Save paths and config names for a short “where” line only when they need to edit something.

## Documents and PRs

Same skim rules for markdown docs, handoffs, and PR descriptions.

Commit subject stays one conventional line. The body may use short bullets.

Do not restyle source files, linters, or diffs for UX.

## Tables

Use tables when comparing options, files, verdicts, or next steps. Keep columns few and headers clear.

## Coding work

When you changed code:

- **What changed**
- **Where** (path)
- **How to see it**
- **What is still open**

Do not recap every tool call.

# Grok Build CLI copy adapter

`grok` 1.0.40 is the Grok Build TUI. It does not auto-load this repo’s `AGENTS.md` (`grok inspect` reported no project instructions). Pasting means passing the text on the command that actually runs.

Do not write `~/.grok/config.toml`. Do not write `~/.config/kilo/`.

## Headless check

From a throwaway directory, not this repo and not the live config:

```text
grok -p "<short status question>" --rules <contents of adapters/tui/AGENTS.md> --max-turns 2 --no-subagents --permission-mode plan
```

`--rules` appends. It does not replace Grok’s own prompt. If the reply is still a telegram, the paste did not win. That is a real result, not a reason to edit the live Kilo window.

`--system-prompt-override` replaces the prompt instead. Use it only when the question is whether this exact text was sent, and say so in the score note.

## Interactive TUI

`grok` with no `-p` opens the TUI. Do not start it against the live Kilo config. A TUI session is not proof of CSS. Score the finished text the same way as `grok -p`: did a question get an answer, in paragraphs, without a px dump.

## What this cannot prove

A CLI reply is not W3C PROV, not the 2026-09-20 session, and not a diff of the live stylesheet.

"""Run portable checkers. No Kilo UI required."""

from __future__ import annotations

import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))

from checkers import hot_reload, routing, tokens, vision, writing  # noqa: E402


def main() -> int:
    total = 0
    for name, mod in [
        ("writing", writing),
        ("routing", routing),
        ("tokens", tokens),
        ("hot-reload", hot_reload),
        ("vision", vision),
    ]:
        print(f"=== {name} ===")
        failed = mod.run()
        total += failed
        print()
    if total:
        print(f"{total} FAILED")
        return 1
    print("ALL PORTABLE CHECKERS PASSED")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

# Project Continuity Modules

Project Continu
ity Modules (PCM) is a Git-native continuity 
system for long-running work with AI agents.


It exists for a simple reason: **a project c
an last for months, but an agent session does
 not.**

## The problem PCM is trying to solv
e

Working with capable agents is easy when t
he task fits inside one conversation. Long-ru
nning projects are different.

Over time, imp
ortant context gets spread across chat histor
ies, local notes, branches, issue comments, g
enerated summaries, and the memory of whichev
er person or agent was working last. Eventual
ly the project starts depending on a particul
ar session still being available and correctl
y remembered.

That creates a few recurring p
roblems.

### Context rot

Long conversations
 gradually become poor project memory.

Early
 decisions fall out of the active context win
dow. Summaries compress away details that lat
er turn out to matter. Agents repeat work bec
ause they cannot see what was already tried.

display.text:
# Handoff Protocol

## Goal

A fresh session should resume from repository state without needing the previous conversation.

## Canonical hierarchy

```text
PROJECT
  ↓
CURRENT
  ↓
TASK
  ↓
CHECKPOINTS
```

Issues/Beads/PRs mirror coordination. Context packs are generated views.

## Start-session procedure

1. read `PROJECT.md`;
2. read `checkpoints/CURRENT.md`;
3. open the active task;
4. read only the minimum relevant spec/design file;
5. confirm branch/scope before edits.

## Checkpoint format

Append, do not rewrite history:

```
### YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC — <agent/session>

Completed:
- ...

Evidence:
- command/artifact -> observed result

Decisions:
- ...

Changed:
- ...

Blocked/uncertain:
- none | ...

Next:
- one atomic action
```

## Stop-session requirements

Before stopping:
- commit meaningful work or document dirty state;
- record tests/commands/results;
- record uncertainty rather than guessing;
- set one exact next action;
- update CURRENT only when repository-level state changed;
- link task ID to issue/PR/Beads item when used.

## Context packs

A context pack may concatenate/transform canonical state for convenience, but must identify:
- repository;
- ref/branch;
- commit;
- protocol version;
- task ID;
- generation time;
- source file list.

Never update a context pack instead of canonical state.

# Exportable harness modules — Project Contract

<!-- continuity:project {"id":"exportable-harness-modules","protocol_version":"0.1.0-draft","schema":"project-continuity.project.v1","title":"Exportable harness modules"} -->

## Main goal

Keep the five UX behaviors that made VS Code Kilo usable, so a new config or a TUI can copy them without stripping the live install.

## Why

The live window is the gold after. A later session must be able to resume from this repository, not from a chat that may be gone.

## Scope

The five behavior specs, the known-good copy source, the evidence honesty rules, and a throwaway text-half copy test.

## Non-goals

W3C PROV rewritten from memory. A new export of the 2026-09-21 session unless the owner asks. Ordered diffs of the live Kilo config. Fossil-core ingest. Transcript mining. Editing `~/.config/kilo/` or the installed extension.

## Definition of success

A fresh session can read this contract, the current checkpoint, and the active task, then tell a copy test from a path test without searching the rest of the disk.

+# Exportable harness modules — Project Contract
+
+<!-- continuity:project {"id":"exportable-harness-modules","protocol_version":"0.1.0-draft","schema":"project-continuity.project.v1","title":"Exportable harness modules"} -->
+
+## Main goal
+
+Keep the five UX behaviors that made VS Code Kilo usable, so a new config or a TUI can copy them without stripping the live install.
+
+## Why
+
+The live window is the gold after. A later session must be able to resume from this repository, not from a chat that may be gone.
+
+## Scope
+
+The five behavior specs, the known-good copy source, the evidence honesty rules, and a throwaway text-half copy test.
+
+## Non-goals
+
+W3C PROV rewritten from memory. A new export of the 2026-09-21 session unless the owner asks. Ordered diffs of the live Kilo config. Fossil-core ingest. Transcript mining. Editing `~/.config/kilo/` or the installed extension.
+
+## Definition of success
+
+A fresh session can read this contract, the current checkpoint, and the active task, then tell a copy test from a path test without searching the rest of the disk.

"""Evidence-honesty properties. No UI required."""

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]


def run() -> int:
    fails = 0
    evidence = (ROOT / "pack" / "evidence.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    readme = (ROOT / "README.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    tui = (ROOT / "adapters" / "tui" / "AGENTS.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    opencode = (ROOT / "adapters" / "opencode" / "README.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    grok = (ROOT / "adapters" / "grok" / "README.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")

    checks = [
        (evidence, "Copy test", "E1 names the copy test"),
        (evidence, "Path test", "E1 names the path test"),
        (evidence, "This is not W3C PROV", "E5 refuses a PROV relabel"),
        (evidence, "2026-09-20", "E4 names the export date"),
        (evidence, "2026-09-21", "E4 names the gold-signal date"),
        (evidence, "session_diff", "E3 names the stored diff"),
        (tui, "Chat.", "TUI paste includes routing"),
        (tui, "start with the answer", "TUI paste includes answer-first"),
    ]
    for text, needle, label in checks:
        if needle in text:
            print(f"PASS {label}")
        else:
            print(f"FAIL {label}")
            fails += 1

    if "FOSSIL can answer what we tried" in readme:
        print("FAIL README still claims FOSSIL can answer the whole history")
        fails += 1
    else:
        print("PASS README does not overclaim the history")

    for name, text in (("opencode", opencode), ("grok", grok)):
        if "~/.config/kilo/" in text and "Do not" in text:
            print(f"PASS {name} adapter forbids the live Kilo config")
        else:
            print(f"FAIL {name} adapter missing live-config refusal")
            fails += 1

    return fails

With this config, `grok` runs your auth binary, stores the token, and routes inference through your corporate proxy. See [Authentication](#authentication) for full auth setup details.

---

## AGENTS.md

Add project-specific instructions by creating an agent rules file (e.g., `AGENTS.md`). Grok reads these files and appends their contents to the system prompt.

Grok scans for agent rules in this order:

1. `~/.grok/` (global rules)
2. If inside a git repo: every directory from the repo root → current working directory (inclusive)
3. If **not** inside a git repo: only the current working directory

Within each directory, Grok checks for these filenames:

- `Agents.md`, `Claude.md`, `AGENT.md`, `AGENTS.md`

Ordering matters: files found later (deeper directories) come last, so they effectively take precedence if instructions conflict. Files ignored by gitignore are skipped. Each file is capped at 10,000 characters (truncated with a warning if exceeded).

> **Note:** The `--rules` flag appends _additional_ rules on top of any discovered agent files, so you can combine both for session-specific customization.

---

## Skills

Skills are reusable prompt packages that extend Grok with specialized workflows, domain knowledge, and tool integrations. Use them to encode repeatable procedures that would otherwise require re-explaining each session.

### Skill Locations

Grok discovers skills from these directories (in priority order):

| Location                    | Scope | Priority |
| --------------------------- | ----- | -------- |
| `./.grok/skills/`           | Local | Highest  |
| `<repo_root>/.grok/skills/` | Repo  | Medium   |
| `~/.grok/skills/`           | User  | Lowest   |
| `~/.claude/skills/`         | User  | Lowest   |

Skills with the same name are deduplicated — higher priority locations override lower ones.

Repo-scoped skills (Local and Repo) respect `.gitignore` and are filtered out if ignored. User-scoped skills (`~/.grok/skills/`) are outside the repo and never filtered.

### Configuration

Add extra skill directories or exclude paths via `[skills]` in config.toml:

```toml
[skills]
paths = ["~/my-team-skills"]          # additional directories to scan
ignore = ["~/my-team-skills/wip"]     # paths to exclude
```

### Creating a Skill

Each skill lives in its own directory with a `SKILL.md` file:

```
~/.grok/skills/
└── commit/
    └── SKILL.md
```

**SKILL.md format:**

```markdown
---
name: commit
description: Create well-formatted git commits following conventional commit standards. Use when the user wants to commit changes or asks for /commit.
---

# Git Commit Skill

display.text:
## Agent Profiles

Agent profiles control the system prompt, toolset, and behavior of a session. A profile is a `.md` file with YAML frontmatter, or a named agent discovered from disk.

Grok discovers agent definitions from `.grok/agents/` (project), `~/.grok/agents/` (user), and built-in agents. Priority (highest wins):

1. `--agent-profile <PATH>` CLI flag
2. `[agent]` section in `config.toml`
3. `GROK_AGENT` env var
4. Default `grok-build` agent

```toml
# ~/.grok/config.toml
[agent]
name = "my-custom-agent"             # Discovered by name
# definition = "/path/to/agent.md"   # OR: explicit path
```

```bash
grok --agent-profile ./my-agent.md
# or
export GROK_AGENT="my-custom-agent"
```

---

## Subagents

Subagents spawn independent child sessions that handle tasks in parallel. Each child has its own context window and can optionally inherit the parent's conversation history. Enabled by default.

### Disabling

```bash
export GROK_SUBAGENTS=0              # Environment variable
```

```toml
# ~/.grok/config.toml
[subagents]
enabled = false
```

### Toggles and Model Overrides

Disable specific subagent types while keeping the system enabled, or route them to different models:

```toml
[subagents.toggle]
explore = true                       # default — omitted agents are enabled
plan = false                         # disable plan subagent

[subagents.models]
explore = "grok-build"              # route explore to a lighter model
```

By default a subagent inherits the parent session's model. Only an explicit
per-agent pin overrides that: `[subagents.models].<agent>` (highest priority),
then the agent definition's `model`. Both pins apply unconditionally,
regardless of which model the parent is on.

### Roles and Personas

Roles define reusable capability/model defaults. Personas layer tone and behavior instructions onto the child prompt.

```toml
[subagents.roles.researcher]
description = "Deep research agent"
default_capability_mode = "read-only"
model = "grok-build"
prompt_file = ".grok/prompts/researcher.md"

I have a solid picture. The user asked how to use Kilo outputs/transcripts as golden behavior and compare against grok, opencode, pi, and configure adapters rather than just copying the file.
To use Kilo’s outputs and transcripts as the golden standard, we treat the actual prompt that Kilo sent (pulled from AGENTS.md + agent-prompt.txt) plus the scored properties (routing, writing style, answer-first, no forced TL;DR, etc.) as the reference. We then run the same 5–10 frozen asks against Grok, OpenCode Pi, and the other harnesses in throwaway configs so we can diff behavior instead of trying to copy prose.

For each harness we override the winning layer rather than hoping a markdown file will be read:

- Grok: we create or edit an agent-profile that 1) forces the system prompt to contain Kilo-style routing and writing rules and 2) explicitly says it wins over “complete the task”. We run it with `--agent-profile` on a temp file so the default Grok prompt never leaks in.

- OpenCode: we spin up a throwaway opencode.json that sets `agent.prompt` to the Kilo-style instruction string and overrides the build agent’s default so it doesn’t inherit the live global AGENTS.md or the permission: allow setting. We also point it at a temp project dir so the live ~/.config/opencode is untouched.

**Kilo’s sentences are not the gold. The behavior is.** A later harness should get the same short asks, and be scored on whether a question got an answer in real paragraphs. Matching Kilo word for word is the wrong test, and dropping the same markdown file into another product is not an adapter. We already saw that fail.

The live VS Code Kilo is the gold after, because you said that window works. What made it work is two layers, and both have to be the text that is actually sent. One is the instruction file loaded every turn. The other is the agent prompt set on `build`, `code`, `plan`, and `general`, so the product’s terse “just do the task” default loses. The stylesheet does not transfer to a terminal. The 2026-09-20 transcript is not that day’s reply gold, and it is not a set of expected answers.

A fair compare is a small frozen ask list, not the whole session. Same status question, same “let’s do it” with no go, same short explanation. Capture one reply from the current Kilo window for each ask and keep it as a reference sample. Then run each other harness on a throwaway config, never on the live Kilo install. Score the reply, not the wording: did tools start, does the first sentence state the result, is it paragraphs, is there a forced TL;DR, is there a path or pixel dump. The Kilo reply sits beside that score so a person can see what “good” looked like. It is not a string the other model must reproduce.

What has to change is the prompt that wins, plus the tool policy on a chat turn.

| Product | What actually lost last time | What the adapter has to set |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Kilo, the gold | The default personality, until the overlay was sent every turn | Already done in the live window. Copy that prompt onto a new config only. |
| Grok Build | `--rules` only appends. Grok’s own “complete the task” prompt still won, and tools started. A file in this repo was not loaded, because the project was not trusted. | An agent profile, passed with `--agent-profile`, whose system prompt includes routing and says it wins over the default. Chat turns must not be allowed to open tools. Do not write `~/.grok/config.toml`. |
| OpenCode | Project `AGENTS.md` loaded, and so did the global one. `opencode run` used the build agent, and permissions were allow, so it ran shell commands before answering. | A throwaway project config that overrides the build agent prompt, or a named chat agent selected with `--agent`. The global file must not be the thing under test. Do not edit `~/.config/opencode/`. |
| Pi | The home directory only has a model provider file. No instruction surface was found. | Do not invent keys. Find the prompt Pi actually sends. If it has none, it cannot take this behavior. |

The last run is the proof that a copy is not a configuration. Grok received the paste and still said it would go check. OpenCode answered only after tools. The next adapter is a profile that replaces the winning prompt and blocks a tool start on a status question, then the same three asks again. That work is not started.
